Thecast-grown monocrystaline-like silicon (mono-like Si) technology has been reactivated recently for the manufacture of high-efficiency solar cells at low cost. In this paper,we have provided a progressive research, both experimentallyand theoretically,to improve the efficiencyof mono-like Si pasivated emitter and rearcells (PERCs) through production lines.By employing rear surface passivation of $\mathrm { A l O _ { x } / t r i p l e { - } S i N _ { x } { : } H }$ layers,the average efficiency has increased to $2 1 . 8 7 \%$ with a champion efficiency of $2 2 . 3 2 \%$ from the standard mono-like Si PERCs of $2 1 . 7 2 \%$ efficiency with $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ capped with double $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } ; H }$ layers.We have further optimized the rear electrode contact patterns and introduced the selective emiter (SE) technology,yieldingan absolute efficiency improvement of $0 . 1 9 \%$ and $0 . 2 6 \%$ ,respectively.Integrating all approaches of the triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } \mathrm { : H } }$ ，rear contact patern optimization and SE technology,we have demonstrated that the mono-like Si PERCs can reach the average efficiency of $2 2 . 2 \%$ with a maximum efficiency of $2 2 . 5 \%$ ，similar to the current Czochralski monocrystalline Si counterparts.
1． Introduction

For the recent five years, there is a growing tendency of crystalline silicon solar cells that the conventional aluminum back surface field (Al-BSF)design is in a transition to passivated emitter and rear cells (PERCs).It is expected that the production capacity of PERCs will be over10oGWp in China by the end of 2019,and nowadays PERCs have become the mainstream of the highly competitive photovoltaic (PV) market.The concept of PERCs was first proposed by Blakers et al.[1],in 1989.In the past 3O years,a significant subsequent motivation for the shift from conception to mass production is associated with the rapid development of manufacturing technologies [2,3],e.g.,rear dielectric coating [4,5],wet chemical polishing etch [6] and laser-based selective emitter (SE)[7] and contact ablation [8].An aluminium oxide/silicon nitride $( \mathrm { A l _ { 2 } O _ { 3 } / S i N _ { x } { : } H } )$ structure was proposed for the rear passivation in 2009[9,1O],which has long been adopted in the industry until now.In our previous work,a feasible silicon oxide $\mathrm { ( S i O _ { 2 } ) }$ passivation technique for industry-related PERCs was also investigated [1l] as a way of improving the long-wavelength response and reducing rear surface recombination.In 2011,a $1 9 . 5 \%$ cell efficiency of multicrystalline silicon (mc-Si) PERCs was achieved by Q-Cells [12].Next year,Suntech

Power successfully manufactured advanced PERCs with a laser-based SE [13],instead of other complicated approaches such as ion implantation [14] and printable dopant [15].While LONGi Solar has declared the realization of world-record PERC efficiency of $2 4 . 0 6 \%$ in 2019 [16], the average efficiency for Czochralski monocrystalline silicon ( $\mathrm { \Delta C z }$ mono-Si) PERCs in current mass production is in the range of $2 2 . 2 \pm 0 . 2 \%$

It should be noted that the PV industry as a whole is dominated by $\mathbf { { C } } \mathbf { { Z } }$ mono-Si PERCs due to in principle the reduced cell efficiency of mc-Si PERCs as well as their limited space to improve the efficiency [17]. Nevertheless,another challenge is indispensable,originating from the fact that the cost of Cz mono-Si wafers is still $3 0 { - } 4 0 \%$ higher than that of mc-Si ones at the present stage [18],causing a significant influence on the price of high-efficiency PERCs.This is unfavorable for the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) and resolutely enhancing PERC efficiency without increasing the cost should be a decisive strategy.In this situation,the ever popular cast-grown monocrystalline-like silicon (mono-- like Si) technology in 2O1O has been reactivated [19],which was first proposed by Ciszek et al.[2O],in 1979.The rapid development of mono-like Si wafers provides the possibility to fabricate high-efficiency PERCsata relatively low cost.Since 2Ol7,a great variety of works has been carried out to investigate the growth and material features of mono-like Si,e.g.,impact of impurities [21],defect-related recombination [22] and dislocations [23].Liu et al.[24],proposed a phosphorous diffusion process to improve the electronic quality of highly defective mono-like Si.Lan et al.[25],introduced a simple approach to control the ingot quality and cell appearance of mono-like Si.Particularly,GCL Poly has played a significant role in the research and development of mono-like Si material,which is strongly supported by several solar cell manufacturing companies.In 2Ol9,Canadian Solar has reported the world-record efficiency of $2 2 . 2 8 \%$ for the mono-like Si PERCs [26].As a promising alternative to the conventional Cz mono-Si PERCs, the production capacity of mono-like Si PERCs is expected to reach 6GWp in 2019 with an average efficiency of $2 1 . 8 \pm 0 . 2 \%$ in mass production currently [27].

text: In contrast to the quick pushing in the PV industry,there is almost no relative report on the mono-like Si PERCs in academia,except three proceedings papers by Xu etal. [28],by Dullweber et al.[29],in 2013 and by Chang et al.,in 2O14 [3O],respectively.We notice that the record cellsachieved by either LONGi Solar or Canadian Solar were only certified by the third-party laboratory without any technical analysis. This paper is aimed at providing a progressive research,both experimentally and theoretically, to extend the overall efficiency of mono-like Si PERCs through the production lines.Based on the standard PERCs with $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ capped by double $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ layers at the rear surface with the average efficiency of $2 1 . 7 2 \%$ ，we have integrated the optimized rear $\mathrm { A l O _ { x } / t r i p l e { \mathrm { - } } S i N _ { x } { \mathrm { : } } H }$ passivation and contact patterns with front laser-based SE technology.With our choice of these feasible technologies,the average efficiency of mono-like Si PERCs has reached $2 2 . 2 \%$ ， with a champion efficiency of $2 2 . 5 \%$ ,which is almost the same as the $\mathbf { { C } } \mathbf { { Z } }$ mono-Si counterparts.
2.Experimental and simulation

We fabricated three types of PERC structures,i.e.,standard PERC (baseline with conventional double- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } ; H }$ passivation layers),PERC with triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } ; H }$ passivation layers (shortened as triple- $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H ) } }$ and PERC with integration of the SE technology (shortened as SE).The wafers used for this work were p-type mono-like Si wafers with a ${ < } 1 0 0 { > }$ grain orientation,a size of $1 5 7 . 7 5 \times 1 5 7 . 7 5 \mathrm { { m m } ^ { 2 } }$ ，a thickness of $1 8 0 \pm 2 0 \mu \mathrm { m }$ and a resistivity of about $0 . 8 \Omega \mathrm { c m }$ .Fig.1 illustrates the

PERC structures and the corresponding fabrication processes,together with the details of rear $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ and $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ layers as well as the front $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ antireflection coating (ARC) layer.
2.1．Standard baseline PERCs

The wafers underwent the following production line treatments: 1) standard damage etching,wet-chemical alkaline texturing like $\mathrm { c z }$ wafers to achieve the random pyramid texture with a lower reflectance compared to acidic texturing,which is considered to be more advisable for mc-Si wafers with random grain orientations [31],and RCA clean (InOxSide,RENA); 2) diffusion using $\mathrm { P O C l } _ { 3 }$ as precursor gas to form $n ^ { + }$ emitter with the sheet resistance $( R _ { \mathrm { s h } } )$ of approximately $7 0 \Omega / \boxed { }$ (M5111-4WL/UM,CETC 48th Research Institute); 3) edge isolation, rear side polishing and removal of phosphorous silicate glass (PSG） in $\mathrm { H F / H N O _ { 3 } }$ solution (InOxSide,RENA); 4) thermal oxidation (AS-300E)at the temperature of $6 8 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for 20min;5) the $_ { 6 \mathrm { n m } }$ -thick $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ film by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) on the rear side (ALD,Ideal Energy);6) double $S \mathrm { i N } _ { \mathrm { x } : \mathrm { H } }$ layers deposition with thickness of $8 0 \mathrm { n m }$ on the $n ^ { + }$ emitter surface by plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) system (M82200-6/UM,CETC 48th Research Institute)；7) capped with double $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } : H }$ passivation layers through the same PECVD system with thickness of $1 2 0 \mathrm { n m }$ on the rear side after ALD- $\mathbf { \nabla } \cdot \mathbf { A l O _ { x } }$ deposition; 8) laser ablation with a line pattern to form a local contact opening line width of $4 0 { \pm } 2 \mu \mathrm { m }$ (DR-LA-Y40,DR Laser), screen printing (PV120o,DEK) and co-firing technique (CFSeries,Despatch) to ensure front and rear side metallization.
2.2.Triple $\it { . S i N _ { x } . H }$ PERCs

The fabrication of triple ${ \cdot } s \mathrm { i } \mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ PERCs was similar to that of the baseline ones,except for the step 7in Section 2.1.Note that the initial overlapping $1 2 0 \mathrm { n m } \mathrm { S i N _ { x } \mathrm { : } H }$ films on the rear surface of baseline PERCs can be divided into the inner $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ layer with a thickness of $3 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and arefractive index of 2.37 (at $\lambda = 6 3 2 \mathrm { n m }$ ）while the outer $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ layer with a thickness of $9 0 \mathrm { n m }$ andarefractive indexof 2.o9.The different procedures during rear $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H } }$ deposition of triple- $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H } }$ PERCs are as follows:1) keep the inner $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ layer fixed; 2) reduce the thickness of initial outer $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H } }$ layer from $9 0 \mathrm { n m }$ to $4 0 \mathrm { n m }$ ,asanew middle layer with a refractive index of 2.15;3)add another $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ layer as a new outer layer with a thickness of $5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and a refractive index of 1.92. The thickness and refractive index of the overlapping $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H } }$ films were optimized by Wafer Ray Tracer software (PV Lighthouse) [32].

text: 2.3．SE PERCs

The manufacturing processes of SE PERCs were identical to those of the baseline ones,except for the emitter formation procedure,which involved an additional step: laser doping (DR-LA-Y40,DR Laser) performed onwafers after $\mathrm { P O C l } _ { 3 }$ diffusion and followed by the removal of PSG.Laser doping was included to achieve so-called highly doped emitters $( n ^ { + + }$ emitters)and lightly doped emitters $( n ^ { + }$ emitters), leading to the formation of emitters selectively.Among them,PSG produced during $\mathrm { P O C l } _ { 3 }$ diffusion served as a doping source.The $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter was $6 0 { \pm } 5 \Omega / \boxed { \bigtriangledown }$ while the $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of the $n ^ { + }$ emitter was $1 2 0 \pm 1 0 \Omega /$ □
2.4.Symmetrical samples for passivation characteristics

Both saturation current density $\left( J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } } \right)$ and effective minority carrier lifetime $( \tau _ { \mathrm { e f f } } )$ effectively investigate the passivation quality of solar cells in the form of symmetrical structures.For baseline PERCs,the $J _ { 0 e }$ experiment was divided into two parts: the passivation zone and the metal zone.Regarding the passivation zone, $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ passivation layers were deposited on both the textured and phosphorus-diffused surfaces of wafers,with $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of $7 0 \Omega / \Omega ,$ which forms the symmetrical $\mathrm { { S i N _ { x } \mathrm { { : H / S i / } } } }$ $\mathrm { S i N _ { x } : H }$ structure.Prior to $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x } \mathrm { { : } H } }$ deposition, textured and diffused wafers underwent the conventional HF cleaning and thermal oxidation processes.The wafers were further treated with sintering process without metallization.Regarding the metal zone,prior to sintering process,the textured and diffused wafers underwent the similar processing sequence as mentioned above,together with Ag printing on both full-area surfaces verse sintering process,with the symmetrical $\mathsf { A g / S i N _ { x } }$ ： $\mathrm { H } / \mathrm { S i } / \mathrm { S i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { \mathrm { : } \mathrm { H } } / \mathrm { A g }$ structure.After that, the wafers were soaked in aqua regia solution $\mathrm { ( H C l { : } H N O _ { 3 } = 3 { : } 1 } ^ { \cdot }$ ）to remove the $\mathbf { A } \mathbf { g }$ paste. As for the $\tau _ { \mathrm { e f f } }$ measurement, the sequence is the same as the $J _ { 0 e }$ experiment for the passivation zone with a symmetrical $\mathrm { S i N _ { x } \mathrm { : H / S i / S i N _ { x } \mathrm { : H } } }$ structure.

For SE PERCs, the $J _ { 0 e }$ experiment was divided into three parts: the $n ^ { + }$ emitter zone, the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter zone and the metal zone.Regarding the $n ^ { + }$ emitter zone,the fabrication of symmetrically structured samples was similar to that of the samples tested for the passivation zone of baseline PERCs,except for the $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of about $1 2 5 \Omega / \boxed { \mathrm { U } }$ Regarding the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter zone, prior to $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ deposition,full-area laser doping was added to the fabrication process on both surfaces of textured and phosphorusdiffused wafers as mentioned above,with $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of $6 5 \Omega / \Omega ,$ the other steps were exactly the same.Regarding the metal zone,the samples just used to test for the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter zone underwent the similar treatments as the metal zone of baseline.For the measurement of $\tau _ { \mathrm { e f f } } ,$ $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ films were deposited on both surfaces of the textured and phosphorus-diffused wafers,with $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ of $1 2 5 \Omega / \Omega ,$ similar to the process as mentioned above.
2.5.Characterization

The thickness and refractive index of $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ and $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ films were measured by spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE400adv-PV).The microgram of different rear contact patterns were obtained by a 3D microscope (Zeta-20,ZETA Instruments).Dopant concentration profiles of the emitters were determined by electrochemical capacitance voltage (ECV) profiling (CVP21,WEP).Sheet resisitance $R _ { \mathrm { s h } }$ and resistivity of the wafers were investigated by four-point probes (28OI Series,Four Dimensions Inc.). The interstitial oxygen $\left( \mathrm { O } _ { \mathrm { i } } \right)$ of the mono-like Si wafers was investigated by FTIR (Bruker IFS-113v). $\tau _ { \mathrm { e f f } } , J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ and implied open circuit voltage $( V _ { \mathrm { o c } } )$ of the emitters were measured by a quasi-steadystate photoconductance(QSSPC） tester (WCT-120， Sinton Instruments).The reflectance and quantum eficiency of solar cells were measured by QEX10 (PV Measurements) system. Finally, the efficiency of the solar cells was tested under AM1.5 spectrum at $2 5 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ by Halm 3600 in the production line.

3．Results and discussion
3.1.Baseline mono-like Si PERCs

Before presenting the results of baseline mono-like Si PERCs,the intrinsic properties of Cz mono-Si and mono-like Si wafers were compared,both experimentally and simulatively.We show in Fig.2(a) the resistivity distribution of these two types of wafers.There is an evident fluctuation found in the resistivity of Cz mono-Si wafers ranging from $0 . 5 \Omega \mathrm { c m }$ to $1 . 3 \Omega \mathrm { c m }$ ,while the concentrated resistivity of monolike Si wafers with a stable value of $0 . 8 0 \pm 0 . 1 \Omega \mathrm { c m }$ is more preferable for the PERC production process.As illustrated in Fig.2(b),we make a comparison between Cz mono-Si PERCs and mono-like Si PERCs with the same cell structure in efficiency and free energy loss analysis (FELA) by Quokka 2 simulation.It is worthy to mention that the measured bulk lifetime was used for the simulation,with a real value of $1 5 0 \mu s$ for monolike Si wafers and $2 0 0 \mu s$ for Cz mono-Si wafers.According to the simulation results,it is found that the energy loss of $\mathrm { c z }$ mono-Si PERCs is lower than that of mono-like Si PERCs,leading to a cell eficiency improvement of $0 . 0 3 \%$ .The main reason lies in the higher bulk recombination of mono-like Si PERCs.However,mono-like Si wafers exhibit much lower $\mathrm { O _ { i } }$ with the value of $6 . 3 4 \mathrm { p p m a }$ ，while the $\mathrm { O _ { i } }$ of $\mathbf { { C } } \mathbf { { Z } }$ mono-Si wafers is 15.43ppma as listed in the left graph of Fig.2(c). The lower $\mathrm { O _ { i } }$ in mono-like Si wafers is instrumental in reducing the lightinduced degradation (LID) [29] of PERC modules.The right graph of Fig.2(c) depicts the mass production efficiency distribution of the baseline mono-like Si PERCs with the manufacturing process flow listed in Fig.1.It is found that the cell efficiency $\left( \eta \right)$ is mainly concentrated at $2 1 . 8 0 \%$ with a share of $2 5 \%$ ,the efficiency of $2 1 . 9 \%$ second,yielding an average $\eta$ of $2 1 . 7 2 \%$ .There is only $1 2 . 6 \%$ share with the $\eta$ of more than $2 2 . 0 \%$ ,indicating the large improvement room for the mono-like Si
PERCs as compared with the Cz mono-Si counterparts.

It is well known that the loss of solar cells could be categorized as optical and electrical losses.Fig.2(d) shows the related losses from a series of simulations to straightforwardly clarify the direction of improvement. On the one hand, the optical losses by Wafer Ray Tracer software indicate that the reflection loss is the dominating factor to limit the carrier collection of solar cells,and the improvement of spectral response is restricted unless the rear films are optimized with an alternative routine for a long optical transmission length.The absorption loss from rear cell is also higher than that of front cell,causing a negative influence on the long-wavelength response.On the other hand,electrical losses with the help of Quokka 2 simulation reveal the serious front emitter loss,which could be effectively reduced by the SE technology. Apart from the Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) loss,the loss from contactat BSF also accounts for a considerable proportion,which can be reduced by optimal rear laser cut groove to achieve a low resistive and recombination loss.The above simulation results guide us to investigate the influence of emitter and rear structure on cell performance below.
3.2.Effect of rear triple $S i N _ { x }  – H$ passivation films

$\left( I _ { \mathrm { s c } } \right)$ .To further improve the long-wavelength response of cells,it is necessary forrear passivation films to obtain a higher reflection when light arrives at the rear,leading more long-wavelength photons to be reflected into the Si wafers to be fully utilized again.According to the reflection theory, triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } : H }$ instead of conventional double ${ \cdot } s \mathrm { i } \mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ in the industry (i.e., the baseline) can effectively increase the reflection because of their multiple surfaces,so that the light fraction has another chance to enter the wafers [34].Prior to the experiments,it is essential to figure out the optimal thickness and refractive index for triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } : H }$ PERCs by means of simulation.Here,the thickness distribution of each $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x } \mathrm { { : } H } }$ layer from the inner to the outer was categorized as two types: $3 0 \mathrm { n m } / 3 0 \mathrm { n m } / 6 0 \mathrm { n m }$ and $3 0 \mathrm { n m } / 4 0 \mathrm { n m } / 5 0 \mathrm { n m }$ ,while the thickness distribution of Obvious differences could be observed in Fig.3(b) between triple-$\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ and baseline PERCs from the absorption and reflection in the long wavelength from $9 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ to $1 2 0 0 \mathrm { n m }$ by Wafer Ray Tracer software.The surface of light propagation has increased for triple- ${ \cdot } s \mathrm { i } \mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ PERCs,leading to a slight increase in reflection and thereby a lower absorption.Another explanation for the improvement might be that there is an increase in extinction coefficient with increasing ratio of $\mathrm { S i H } _ { 4 }$ to $\mathrm { N H } _ { 3 }$ gas flow [38],resulting in a reduced absorption in the long wavelength of triple ${ \cdot } s \mathrm { i } \mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ PERCs with a lower refractive index of1.92 for outer $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ layer,in contrast to the baseline with a refractive index of 2.09 for outer $\mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ layer.The above argument reveals that the reflection and absorption of long-wavelength photons are significantly modified when the rear surfaces are passivated by triple- $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ films.

Fig.3(d) shows the comparison of electrical parameters between the two types of PERCs. Obviously,the average $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and fill factor $( F F )$ of triple- ${ \cdot } s \mathrm { i } \mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { x } } { : } \mathrm { H }$ PERCs exceed the baseline ones,leading to higher $\eta$ .The average $\eta$ reaches $2 1 . 8 7 \%$ for triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } : H }$ PERCs,accompanied by a corresponding increase of $0 . 1 5 \%$ over baseline ones with an average $\eta$ of $2 1 . 7 2 \%$ ，The increase in the $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $5 0 \mathrm { m A }$ is consistent with the improvement of EQE and reflectance in Fig.3(c). It is also worth to mention that the value of series resistance $\left( R _ { s } \right)$ is $0 . 8 6 ~ \mathrm { m } \Omega$ and $0 . 9 2 ~ \mathrm { m } \Omega$ for triple- $\mathrm { { s i N } _ { x : H } }$ and baseline cases,respectively.We assume that the higher $F F$ in triple- $. \mathrm { s i N } _ { \mathrm { x } }$ :H PERCs is due to a nitrogen-rich filmat the Al/ $\mathrm { S i N _ { x } : H }$ interface because of a lower refractive index [39], resulting in attenuating the corrosion penetration of Al paste and thereby a lower $R _ { s } .$ However,no obvious change occurs in $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ as a result of the equivalent total thickness of $\mathrm { \ s i N _ { x } : H }$ films,meaning that the passivation effect is hardly influenced by the triple-layer films.Therefore,it could be concluded that the increased $\eta$ is practically attributed to the improvement of $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ and $F F$ ,which is mainly affected by the lower refractive index at outer layer, enhanced reflection and reduced absorption in the long wavelength.In summary，the rear triple- $S _ { \mathrm { i N _ { x } } }$ H film structure is confirmed to be a promising solution to enhance the long-wavelength spectral response for PERCs.
3.3.Influence of rear electrode contact pattrns

Since the $\mathrm { \Delta A l O _ { x } / S i N _ { x } { : } H }$ stack is considered as an insulating layer,laser ablation is necessarily required for electrode formation at the rear side, that is,aluminum-silicon contact can be realized in the ablation portion [40,41].There is no doubt that the electrode contact patterns should be well designed.Note that the contact patterns in production lines for baseline PERCs are dotted lines with length of $9 3 8 \mu \mathrm { m }$ and lateral spacing of $1 4 5 \mu \mathrm { m } .$ ,respectively,as shown in Fig.4(a).Here,we define a new quantity,real ratio $( L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ,where $\boldsymbol { L } = \boldsymbol { L } ^ { \mathrm { R } } + \boldsymbol { \bar { L } } ^ { \mathrm { I } } , \boldsymbol { L } ^ { \mathrm { R } }$ is the length, and $L ^ { \mathrm { I } }$ is the lateral spacing),to simplify the line patterns description, fixing the values of longitudinal spacing $6 0 0 \mu \mathrm { m }$ and width $4 0 \mu \mathrm { m }$ ，To investigate the influence of rear contact patterns,a series of PERCs with different real ratios $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ were fabricated in mono-like Si wafers.Fig.4(a) shows the image of rear contact patterns with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ranging from $2 3 . 3 \%$ to $5 3 . 8 \%$ ,and the pattern of baseline $( L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 8 6 . 6 \% )$ is also displayed for comparison.The corresponding ratio of electrode contact area to the total area of rear surface is about $1 . 1 \%$ ， $1 . 8 \%$ ， $2 . 3 \%$ ， $2 . 9 \%$ and $4 . 7 \%$ ， respectively.We aim at obtaining the optimal $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ,which can provide the highest output performance compared with baseline PERCs.

The relative values of experimental parameters ( $\Delta V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ ， $\Delta I _ { \mathrm { s c . } }$ ， $\Delta F F$ and $\Delta \eta )$ between four set samples $( L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 2 3 . 3 \%$ ， $3 4 . 4 \%$ ， $4 3 . 4 \%$ and $5 3 . 8 \%$ and baseline are illustrated in Fig.4(b). It is easy to find that with the increase of $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ,the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ diminished progressively.By contrast, obvious improvement in $F F$ is observed with increasing $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ .The $R _ { s }$ of every set sample $( 2 3 . 3 \%$ ， $3 4 . 4 \%$ ， $4 3 . 4 \%$ ， $5 3 . 8 \%$ and $8 6 . 6 \%$ )is 0.92,0.78,0.69, 0.66 and $0 . 6 0 ~ \mathrm { m } \Omega$ ,respectively.The lower the $R _ { s } ,$ the larger the $F F$ ,thus the decline of $F F$ is a result of the increasing $R _ { s } ,$ which is mainly affected by contact resistance and lateral transport resistance [42,43].The above trends can be adequately explained by the dependence of lateral transport resistance on $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ，which follows the adverse tendency as $F F$ However,an increase in the contact area means a reduction in the passivation area [44],causing the $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ to drop clearly.Hence,it is not preferable to improve the performance by increasing the laser cut groove area. One can see that the $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of the four set samples exceed the baseline significantly.There isa nearly 47,81,59 and $4 1 \mathrm { m A }$ improvement with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ of $2 3 . 3 \%$ ， $3 4 . 4 \%$ ， $4 3 . 4 \%$ and $5 3 . 8 \%$ ，respectively,and this could be attributed to differences between current transmission channels and current collection at the rear surface.Also,a homologous trend can be observed in $\eta$ that the conversion efficiency of four set samples is greatly better than the baseline absolutely increased by $0 . 0 9 \%$ ， $0 . 1 9 \%$ ， $0 . 0 8 \%$ and $0 . 0 8 \%$ ,respectively.It indicates that the higher $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and greater $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ would compensate the $F F$ loss accounting for the fact that the sample with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ of $3 4 . 4 \%$ exhibits the best electrical performance in comparison with other set samples.

Fig.4(b)also shows the simulated electrical parameters by Quokka 2 software for verification.In order to ensure an effective and feasible simulation, the experimental data was adopted in the calculation, such as sheet resistance, junction depth,contact resistance, $J _ { 0 \mathrm { { e } } }$ and so on. Note that trends of $\Delta V _ { \mathrm { o c } } ,$ $\Delta I _ { \mathrm { s c } } ,$ △FF and $\Delta \eta$ depicted by Quokka 2 with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ varied from $2 3 . 3 \%$ to $5 3 . 8 \%$ are in good agreement with those through experiments. Simulation results reveal that $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of the $2 3 . 3 \%$ set samples is better than that of the $3 4 . 4 \%$ set ones.This may be due to the identical contact resistivity of rear side selected for each set samples during the simulations.Indeed, the smaller the $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ ，the lower the contact resistivity [45]. Overall,compared with the simulated baseline counterparts,the optimal results of the electrical performance are obtained by Quokka 2at $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 3 4 . 4 \%$ with an absolute increase in efficiency $\eta$ of $0 . 2 3 \%$ ，while the maximum improvement $\eta$ of $0 . 1 9 \%$ has been achieved experimentally for the PERCs with real ratio $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ of $3 4 . 4 \%$

In order to evaluate the improvements of $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ more convincingly, Fig.4(c) depicts EQE spectra of all these set samples.One can clearly observe that the set samples with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 3 4 . 4 \%$ exhibit a stronger spectral response in the long wavelength but nearly no difference in the short and middle wavelength compared with other set samples.This could be associated with the sufficiently high quality of rear surface passivation and good ability of rear current collection,rather than the influence of the emitter and the base.What's more,the EQE tendency of these five set samples is in accordance with the corresponding experimental $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ listed in Fig.4(b).

To straightforwardly analyze the influence of real ratio $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ on electrical losses,the FELA was also carried out by Quokka 2,as illustrated in Fig.4(d).According to the FELA, these five set samples are obviously different in two items,the recombination loss and the resistivity loss of contact in BSF.This is because the higher $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ of rear contact area indicates that the wafer is subject to higher surface recombination velocity as well as greater laser damage,leading to more serious recombination losses of contact in BSF.However, the smaller $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } /$ L of rear contact area possesses a higher transverse resistance,resulting in much more losses.It is required to make a trade-off between the reduction ofresistivity lossand combination loss[42]，and $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 3 4 . 4 \%$ is confirmed to satisfy above requirements commendably. In conclusion,optimal rear electrode contact pattern should not only have high quality passivation,but also low transverse resistance. Too large and too small $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ are not advisable to improve the performance of the PERCs with the following two reasons: (i) the decrease of $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ is inevitable owing to the loss of passivation regions and enhanced absorption of photons by the electrode contact when $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ is too large; (ii) the decline of FF resulting from the excessive $R _ { s }$ appears as well as the deterioration of aluminum-silicon contact performance when $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L$ is too small.

From the FELA in Fig.4(d),one can also note that the top-three energy losses for PERCs are the emitter resistance loss,the SRH bulk recombination loss and the emitter recombination loss.Therefore, the SE technology is a necessary and cost-effective strategy to further optimize the performance of PERC cells,which will be discussed in Section 3.4.
3.4.Analysis of SE technology

Great efforts have been made on optimizing the manufacturing process through production lines with regard to rear sides of the PERCs in our previous sections.Here we will investigate the gains from the front sides combined with SE technology.SE is a structure in which an $n ^ { + + }$ emitter is formed at the front metal finger,together with an $n ^ { + }$ emitter to remain high quality passivation.On the one hand,the $n ^ { + }$ emitter has a completely lower dopant concentration and junction depth,which contributes to less serious recombination in the nonmetallized areas,i.e.,the Auger recombination and SRH recombination [46]. On the other hand, the higher dopant concentration of the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter form high-performance Ohmic contact among the emitter and metal electrodes to reduce the contact resistance [47].

The loss from the cell front was mainly atributed to two components:dielectric and contact areas.It's clear that recombination from the contact between baseline and SE technology is almost the same, which means that recombination from the dielectric areas might be the primary determinant of the emitter quality.

There is now a general consensus that the improvement in $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ is significantly correlated with the rewarding chemical passivation [49].The higher $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ is due to the reduced emitter recombination to the profitable impact of the short-wavelength spectral response.The maximum $\eta$ improvement of $0 . 2 6 \%$ has been obtained on the PERCs combined with SE technology.

In order to further quantitatively explore front emitter quality of both cells,we constituted a valid comparison of recombination current density $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ to evaluate with different regions,i.e.,the metal zone, the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter zone,the $n ^ { + }$ emitter zone for the SE case,and the metal zone, the non-metal zone for the baseline one,respectively.It is worth to mention that $J _ { 0 e }$ of different regions were measured with the symmetrical structures (see section 2.4 for details).Here,the proportion of each region to the total area of cells is also displayed for the purpose of calculating the total recombination current density of cells,as given in Fig.5(e) (the left graph).Note that the $J _ { 0 \mathrm { { e } } }$ of the SE case in three regions (including $n ^ { + }$ emitter, $n ^ { + + }$ emitter and metal) is 48,130 and $9 0 7 \mathrm { f A } /$ $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ , whose area accounts for $9 0 . 6 \%$ ， $5 . 4 \%$ and $4 . 0 \%$ ,respectively, while the $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ of the baseline case in two regions (including non-metal and metal) is $1 0 1 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ and $7 9 6 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ ，accounting for $9 6 \%$ and $4 \%$ ， respectively.The presence of SE technology results ina higher level of $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ in the metal regions.This may be understood by the fact that metal contact of the SE case is performed in the $n ^ { + + }$ emitter region, that is to say the dopant concentration of SE metal regions is higher in comparison with that of the baseline.Another explanation might be that the SE front surface would suffer unavoidable damage caused by the laser doping, thereby resulting in the increase of the Auger recombination in the emitter.

The total $J _ { 0 e }$ of both cells was calculated as a function of $J _ { 0 e }$ of different regions as well as the corresponding area ratios.In other words, the total $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ of the SE case is the sum of the $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ of three areas $( n ^ { + }$ emitter, $n ^ { + + }$ emitter and metal) multiplied by the respective area ratio,while the calculation of the baseline case was similar to that of the SE.Fig.5(e) (the right graph) summarizes the values of the total $J _ { 0 \mathrm { e } }$ for the baseline case of $1 2 8 . 8 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ and for the SE one of $8 6 . 8 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ ，suggesting a good enough front surface passivation.In conclusion,through the integration of SE technology,we have achieved good quality emitter, which is an essential prerequisite for high performance PERCs.

text: 4.Conclusions

In summary,we have investigated both experimentally and theoretically the application of mono-like Si wafers in the mass production of mainstream PERCs.By employing triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } : H }$ in combination with $\mathsf { A l O } _ { \mathbf { x } }$ at the rear surface to replace the standard $\mathbf { A l O _ { x } } ,$ /double- $\mathbf { \mathit { S i N } _ { x } }$ :H stacks,more long-wavelength photons can be reflected into the Si wafers to be utilized again,resulting in an increase in the $I _ { \mathrm { s c } }$ of $5 0 \mathrm { m A }$ The rear triple- $S \mathrm { i N _ { x } ; H }$ also performs a high $F F$ attributed to a nitrogen-rich film at the Al/ ${ } ^ { \prime } \mathrm { S i N } _ { \mathrm { x } : \mathrm { H } }$ interface.Consequently,the average $\eta$ of our mono-like Si PERCs has been increased to $2 1 . 8 7 \%$ from the existing baseline $\eta$ of $2 1 . 7 2 \%$ .We have further demonstrated the effect and role of rear contact patterns,highlighting the necessity of keeping the balance between the passivation and series resistance.The optimal contact pattern of $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } /$ $L = 3 4 . 4 \%$ exhibits a higher performance in both $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ and $I _ { \mathrm { s c } } ,$ and the average $\eta$ increases by more than $0 . 1 9 \%$ absolutely,compared to the standard PERCs with $L ^ { \mathrm { R } } / L = 8 6 . 6 \%$ .Finally,the emitter saturation current density $J _ { 0 \mathrm { { e } } }$ has been dramatically reduced from $1 2 8 . 8 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 }$ to $8 6 . 8 \mathrm { f A } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 }$ by the implementation of SE technology,yielding an absolute average $\eta$ improvement of $0 . 2 6 \%$ .Finally,we have combined these feasible technologies in the process of baseline mono-like Si PERCs.An average $\eta$ of $2 2 . 2 \%$ accompanied by a maximum $\eta$ of $2 2 . 5 \%$ was obtained,which is almost the same as their $\mathrm { c z }$ mono-Si counterparts.
